{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
penguins = pd.read_csv('data/penguins.csv')

# Identify rows with missing flipper_length_mm or body_mass_g
missing_rows = penguins[penguins['flipper_length_mm'].isnull() | penguins['body_mass_g'].isnull()]

# Check if the missing rows are systematically different in sex
# The sex column is missing for both of these rows, so we can't compare
# But we can check if the missing rows are different in species or island
# We already did: they are Adelie (Torgersen) and Gentoo (Biscoe)
# Let's check if the full dataset has a similar distribution

# Full dataset: species and island
full_species = penguins['species'].value_counts(normalize=True)
full_island = penguins['island'].value_counts(normalize=True)

# Missing rows: species and island
missing_species = missing_rows['species'].value_counts(normalize=True)
missing_island = missing_rows['island'].value_counts(normalize=True)

# Compare
print("Full dataset species proportions:")
print(full_species)
print("\nMissing rows species proportions:")
print(missing_species)

print("\nFull dataset island proportions:")
print(full_island)
print("\nMissing rows island proportions:")
print(missing_island)

# Check if the missing rows are outliers in flipper_length_mm or body_mass_g
# But we don't have values for them, so we can't
# Instead, we can check if the remaining data is representative

# Compute correlation on complete cases
complete_data = penguins.dropna(subset=['flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g'])
correlation = complete_data['flipper_length_mm'].corr(complete_data['body_mass_g'])

print(f"\nCorrelation on complete cases: {correlation}")"}
